headline: Dhaka Metro Rail cost to more than double to BDT 2.13 lakh crore; Bangladesh Bank halts Bangabandhu notes
summary: A proposal to increase the cost of two Dhaka metro rail projects to BDT 2.13 lakh crore is awaiting approval. Meanwhile, Bangladesh Bank has stopped issuing notes with Bangabandhu's image, leading to a circulation of older currency.
details: The estimated cost for two Dhaka metro rail projects is set to more than double, from an initial BDT 93,800 crore to a proposed BDT 213,985 crore. This significant increase is currently awaiting approval from the Planning Commission.

Bangladesh Bank has ceased issuing new currency notes featuring Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's image following the July mass uprising. Delays in designing and printing new notes mean older currency dominates circulation, alongside a rise in printing expenses.

An international discussion titled 'Europe and Asia: From Dialogue to a Partnership' was recently hosted by New Delhi's Foreign Correspondents Club (FCC). This event was a joint initiative with the Belgium-based 'Hand in Hand Foundation'.

During his active career, actor Salman Shah had a packed schedule with multiple film shootings and numerous scripts at home. His sudden demise shocked millions of fans and significantly altered the calculations for many film projects.

headline_marked: High Court to [[deliver verdict today in Ashia rape and murder case]]
headline: High Court to deliver verdict today in Ashia rape and murder case
summary: The High Court is set to announce its verdict today on the death reference and appeal of Hitu Sheikh, who was sentenced to death by a lower court for the rape and murder of 8-year-old Ashia in Magura.
details: The High Court is scheduled to announce its verdict today on the death reference and appeal in the rape and murder case of 8-year-old Ashia. Justices Bhishmadev Chakrabortty and K.M. Rasheduzzaman Raja's bench will deliver the judgment on Monday, August 31.
The verdict was previously deferred from August 25. The hearing on the death reference and appeal for the accused concluded on August 23.
Ashia was victimized in March while visiting her sister's in-laws' house in Nij Nanduiali village, Magura. She later died while undergoing treatment at Dhaka's Combined Military Hospital.

Following her death, Ashia's mother filed a case against Hitu Sheikh and three others, all of whom were subsequently arrested by police. The police submitted a chargesheet in the case on April 13, with trial proceedings commencing on April 23 and witness testimonies beginning on April 27.

The Magura Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal previously sentenced the main accused, Hitu Sheikh, to death and fined him one lakh taka. The other three accused in the case were acquitted.
caption:
The High Court is scheduled to deliver its verdict today in the highly anticipated rape and murder case of 8-year-old Ashia.

The High Court is scheduled to announce its verdict today on the death reference and appeal in the rape and murder case of 8-year-old Ashia. Justices Bhishmadev Chakrabortty and K.M. Rasheduzzaman Raja's bench will deliver the judgment on Monday, August 31.

The verdict was previously deferred from August 25. The hearing on the death reference and appeal for the accused concluded on August 23.

Ashia was victimized in March while visiting her sister's in-laws' house in Nij Nanduiali village, Magura. She later died while undergoing treatment at Dhaka's Combined Military Hospital.

Following her death, Ashia's mother filed a case against Hitu Sheikh and three others, all of whom were subsequently arrested by police. The police submitted a chargesheet in the case on April 13, with trial proceedings commencing on April 23 and witness testimonies beginning on April 27.

The Magura Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal previously sentenced the main accused, Hitu Sheikh, to death and fined him one lakh taka. The other three accused in the case were acquitted.
